app.title: LigandNexus
app.summary: A person picks a parent molecule by database ID or by name and checks its structure, with the atoms that can bind a metal highlighted. They pull every database record that contains it as a substructure, from a live chemistry database or an uploaded structure file. In numbered tabs that unlock one after another, they clean the library with rule-based filters, sort each derivative's substituents by functional group and by distance from the binding atom, and pick a representative candidate set balanced between electron-donating and electron-withdrawing groups. At any stage they can score the set against drug-likeness rules and filter on them. They export the chosen set as CSV or Excel, or send it on to build 3D geometries and input files for quantum-chemistry programs.

task.text: Build a small, balanced set of candidate ligands from a parent molecule's database derivatives and hand it on to computational chemistry.

data.text: A library of chemical compounds pulled from a database by substructure search. Each compound has a structure string and computed or downloaded properties. Each compound's substituents are then sorted into categories.
data.item: one derivative compound with its structure string and properties

stage.text: curating a ligand library pulled from a database, before quantum-chemistry calculations

mechanism.text: Tabs run as a pipeline: each step stays disabled until the one before has produced its table, and each shows before/after counts with a bar chart of what was removed or found. A drug-likeness panel can work on the output of any stage. Whatever it leaves on screen is what the export tab offers and what the 3D geometry page can load.

field.text: virtual screening of ligand derivatives in coordination chemistry

workflow.name: narrow a retrieved library to a balanced candidate set and export it

steps.here: Check the parent molecule by database ID or name, then run a substructure search in a chosen database or an uploaded structure file, up to a maximum number of records
Checkboxes drop compounds with metals, salts, net charge, a missing core, or too much mass over the core. Before/after/dropped counts are shown, with a bar chart by reason

steps.step: compute a value from the data
steps.here: Each compound's substituents are cut off at the core and given a functional group and a bond distance to the nearest binding atom. A bar chart shows the most frequent groups
A slider caps the number of candidates. The set is chosen with a minimum and maximum per group-by-position and an optional donor/acceptor balance, with counts of each

steps.step: filter to the items that matter
steps.here: On any stage, compute drug-likeness rules and a blood–brain-barrier estimate, see pass counts as cards, and filter by checkboxes
Choose which stage's table to export, as CSV or as Excel with optional 2D structure images. Or load the set into the 3D page for geometry files and Gaussian/ORCA/Psi4 inputs

distinctive: Substituents are placed by their bond distance from the metal-binding atom (alpha, beta, gamma), not only by what kind of group they are
The candidate selection enforces a minimum share of electron-donating and electron-withdrawing substituents
The rule-based scoring panel can attach to any stage of the pipeline, and what it filters is exactly what gets exported
Data sources range from live database search to downloaded dumps searched locally by substructure
The chosen set can go straight on to force-field 3D geometries and quantum-chemistry input files

parts.title: Coordination analysis tabs
parts.summary: Numbered tabs that unlock in order, carrying the library from retrieval through cleaning, classification and selection to export.

parts.title: Clean the library
parts.summary: Applies checkbox filters for metals, salts, charge, missing core and excess mass, and shows before, after and dropped counts with a bar chart by reason.

parts.title: Classify substituents
parts.summary: Gives each substituent a functional group and a bond distance to the binding atom, then charts the most frequent groups.

parts.title: Select a balanced candidate set
parts.summary: Chooses up to a set number of candidates, with limits per group-by-position and an optional donor/acceptor balance, and reports how many of each type were kept.

parts.title: Drug-likeness panel
parts.summary: Computes drug-likeness rules and a blood–brain-barrier estimate for the chosen stage's compounds, shows pass counts, and filters the set by those criteria.
